questions.question_text:
The cubic $y = x^3$ is translated $5$ units to the right, then vertically dilated by a factor of $7$.
What is the equation of the resulting cubic curve?

options.why: Added $5$ instead of subtracting $5$ for a horizontal translation to the right.
Placed the dilation factor inside the cubing bracket instead of vertically.
Treated the horizontal shift as a vertical translation of $5$ units downward.

questions.question_text:
The graph of $y = \sqrt{x}$ is reflected across the $y$-axis, then translated $6$ units down.
What is the equation of the transformed graph?

options.why: Reflected across the $x$-axis instead of the $y$-axis.
Placed the vertical translation inside the square root under the radical.
Reflected across the $x$-axis and placed the shift under the square root.

questions.question_text:
The curve $y = \dfrac{1}{x}$ is horizontally dilated by a factor of $5$, then translated $4$ units to the right.
What is the equation of the resulting curve?

options.why: Replaced the original input $x$ with $5x - 4$ instead of $\dfrac{x - 4}{5}$, multiplying by $5$ and subtracting $4$ outside that multiplication.
Added $4$ instead of subtracting $4$ for a shift to the right.
Substituted $5x$ instead of $\dfrac{x}{5}$ for horizontal dilation by $5$.

questions.question_text:
The point $P(5, -7)$ lies on $y = f(x)$.
What are the coordinates of the image point $P'$ on the curve $y = 4f(x - 2) + 6$?

options.why: Subtracted $2$ from the $x$-coordinate instead of adding $2$ for $x - 2$.
Subtracted $6$ instead of adding $6$ in the vertical transformation.
Shifted $x$ left to get $5 - 2 = 3$ and incorrectly calculated $4(-7)$ as $-16$, then added $6$ to get $-10$.

questions.question_text:
The point $Q(12, 14)$ lies on $y = f(x)$.
What are the coordinates of the image point $Q'$ on the curve $y = -f\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right) + 5$?

options.why: Divided the $x$-coordinate by $3$ instead of multiplying by the factor $3$.
Subtracted $5$ instead of adding $5$ in $-y + 5$.
Divided $x$ by $3$ and forgot the reflection negative sign on $y$.

questions.question_text:
The graph of $y = \sqrt{x}$ is reflected across the $y$-axis, then translated $7$ units right and $11$ units up.
What is the equation of the transformed graph?

options.why: Omitted the reflection across the $y$-axis.
Translated left by $7$ after the reflection, substituting $x + 7$ into $\sqrt{-x}$.
Translated down by $11$ instead of up.

questions.question_text:
The graph of $y = 5^x$ is vertically dilated by a factor of $2$, reflected across the $x$-axis, then translated $8$ units up.
What is the equation of the transformed graph?

options.why: Omitted the reflection across the $x$-axis.
Translated down by $8$ instead of up.
Applied a horizontal translation left by $8$ instead of a vertical translation up by $8$.

questions.question_text:
The absolute value graph $y = |x|$ is translated $7$ units to the left, vertically dilated by a factor of $3$, and translated $4$ units down.
What is the equation of the resulting graph?

options.why: Subtracted $7$ instead of adding $7$ for a translation to the left.
Used a vertical dilation factor of $\dfrac{1}{3}$ instead of $3$.
Added $4$ instead of subtracting $4$ for a downward translation.

questions.question_text:
The point $M(-6, 13)$ lies on $y = f(x)$.
What are the coordinates of the image point $M'$ on the curve $y = 4f(2x + 8) - 15$?

options.why: Ignored the horizontal dilation factor and solved $x + 8 = -6$ instead of $2x + 8 = -6$.
Added $15$ instead of subtracting it, computing $4(13) + 15$ rather than $4(13) - 15$.
Made both slips: solved $x + 8 = -6$ with no factor of $2$, and computed $4(13) + 15$ instead of $4(13) - 15$.

questions.question_text:
The point $R(-5, 9)$ lies on $y = f(x)$.
What are the coordinates of its image on the curve $y = -3f(2 - 3x) + 7$?

options.why: Ignored the factor of $3$ and solved $2 - x = -5$ instead of $2 - 3x = -5$.
Omitted the vertical reflection and calculated $3(9) + 7 = 34$.
Subtracted $7$ instead of adding it, calculating $-3(9) - 7 = -34$.
